verdict.rationale: dlt pipelines are written as plain Python code (dlt.pipeline/run calls, decorators) that live in the user's own repo, deployable via GitHub Actions/Airflow/serverless, and community feedback confirms the code-first, maintainable nature ('I can do everything via code, which makes things more maintainable'). Config-driven sources (rest_api, sql_database) and declarative schema/config support reinforce portability across environments and destinations without rewriting pipeline code. missing for 10: no explicit independent case study on code review/version-control workflows, and no direct evidence addressing git-based review practices beyond general 'plain Python' framing.
